name: mem-m4-growth-division-propensity
title: Membrane Division: Can a Vesicle Grow and Divide?
honest_caveat: MD tests candidate prebiotic compositions; it does NOT by itself demonstrate endogenous membrane formation. Division PROPENSITY here is a geometry/curvature/barrier measure and is NOT a demonstration of heritable division (that is Gate D's og-34 / template-copying line).
question: Can supplied amphiphiles insert into, reshape, and expand a vesicle - and what is its propensity to divide?
hypothesis: Supplied amphiphiles insert and expand membrane area; area growth drives curvature/shape change and lowers the budding barrier - a propensity to divide, set by composition and osmotic conditions.
experiment: Measure amphiphile insertion/exchange, area growth, curvature change and the budding/division barrier for candidate vesicles - a division PROPENSITY, kept separate from heritable division.
primary_output: Insertion/exchange rates, area-growth trajectories, curvature change, and budding/division barrier estimates.
first_cut_forthcoming: A lightweight amphiphile-insertion / area-growth MD on a preassembled vesicle (planned, not yet scaffolded or named). Soft forward-reference only; hardened later.
extends: og-self-compartmentation (the mem-m1 amphiphile-assembly, mem-m2 permeability/retention, mem-m3 stability arms — folded there)
proposed_acceptance_criteria: Insertion/area-growth/curvature are measured for supplied vs no-supply at identical feeds across vesicle sizes.
A division-propensity bound (toward or away from a division-competent geometry) is reported either way.
The result is reported as a propensity, explicitly NOT as evidence of heredity (og-33 metabolism-driven division and og-34 heredity remain the gate-earning lines).
